::: {.callout-note appearance="simple" icon=false}
**Part IV · Translating models into practice** · **Level:** independent application · **Teaching units:** 25–28
(4 × 45 min) · **Required reading:** core readings of B22 and B23 (about 20 minutes) ·
**Case sheets:** [Tabletop exercise: a dashboard changes purpose](../exercises/casebook-w7-tabletop.qmd) ·
**Legal status:** November 2026
:::

## Guiding question

**When a research dashboard is to be used in care, receives an update and leaks case text, who has to decide what,
on which legal basis, and by when?**

## Learning objectives

By the end of this workshop you can

1. compare two intended purposes of the same software and derive roles and questions under the AI Act, the MDR and,
   where relevant, the IVDR, citing the primary source and marking what is a case assumption and what is *open*;
2. draw separate data flows for care and for later research use and check purpose, legal basis under Article 6
   and exception under Article 9 GDPR, processor contract, retention, rights of the people affected and the DPIA
   threshold;
3. complete a threat model and propose for confidentiality, integrity and availability one control each, a test
   that shows it works and a recovery step;
4. run an incident from containment to restart, deciding notification to the authority (Article 33 GDPR) and
   communication to the people affected (Article 34 GDPR) separately;
5. write a short, honest message to affected patients with a reachable contact.

## Preparation

- **Required reading** (about 20 minutes):
  [B22 · Regulating research software and clinical AI – core reading](https://r-heller.github.io/clinical-data-science-in-r/chapters/b22-regulation.html#sec-b22-core)
  and
  [B23 · Data protection along the entire data flow – core reading](https://r-heller.github.io/clinical-data-science-in-r/chapters/b23-data-protection.html#sec-b23-core).
- **On the table during the exercise:** [B24 · Information security and recovery](https://r-heller.github.io/clinical-data-science-in-r/chapters/b24-information-security-recovery.html)
  and [B25 · Security risks of learning and generative systems](https://r-heller.github.io/clinical-data-science-in-r/chapters/b25-security-risks-ai-systems.html);
  [B21 · Ethics](https://r-heller.github.io/clinical-data-science-in-r/chapters/b21-ethics.html) for the patient
  perspective and [B20 · Pilot operation, impact and monitoring](https://r-heller.github.io/clinical-data-science-in-r/chapters/b20-pilot-operation-monitoring.html)
  for the restart.
- **Guests (proposal):** contributions from data protection, medical device regulation and information security.
  The roles are suggestions; any of them can be played by course participants.

## Teaching units

| Unit | Task | Minutes | Observable evidence |
|---|---|---:|---|
| 25 | Compare two intended purposes and determine roles and questions under the EU AI Act, the MDR or, where relevant, the IVDR. Name one missing manufacturer document ([starting situation](../exercises/casebook-w7-tabletop.qmd#start)). | 45 | A dated regulatory note with primary source, case assumption and open next step. |
| 26 | Design one data flow for care and one for later research use. Check legal basis, health data, processing on behalf, retention, rights of the people affected and the DPIA threshold ([card 1](../exercises/casebook-w7-tabletop.qmd#card-1)). | 45 | A data flow with recipient, purpose, access roles, deletion point and a reasoned DPIA pre-check. |
| 27 | Complete a threat model. For data leaving the system, a manipulated model version and an outage, design one protection, one detection test and one recovery measure each ([card 2](../exercises/casebook-w7-tabletop.qmd#card-2)). | 45 | A control matrix for confidentiality, integrity and availability and a fall-back option tested in the exercise. |
| 28 | Tabletop: synthetic case text is visible in a support log. Contain, secure evidence, alert roles, assess consequences and decide on the restart ([card 3](../exercises/casebook-w7-tabletop.qmd#card-3)). | 45 | An incident log, a reasoned assessment of notification and of communication, the patient perspective and a release criterion. |

## Legal status, November 2026

::: {.callout-important appearance="simple" icon=false}
**Checked against the primary texts on 8 November 2026.** Publication, entry into force and date of application are
kept apart.

- **AI Act**, Regulation (EU) 2024/1689: in force since 1 August 2024. Chapters I and II (including Article 4 on AI
  literacy and the prohibitions in Article 5) have applied since 2 February 2025.
- **Digital Omnibus on AI**, Regulation (EU) 2026/1744 of 8 July 2026: published in the Official Journal on
  24 July 2026, in force since 27 July 2026. It amends, among other things,
  - **Article 4**: providers and deployers now *take measures to support* the AI literacy of their staff and of
    other persons operating AI systems on their behalf; the obligation does not require a specific level of AI
    literacy to be guaranteed;
  - **Article 113**: the requirements of Chapter III Sections 1–3 apply from **2 December 2027** to high-risk
    systems under Article 6(2) and Annex III, and from **2 August 2028** to high-risk systems under Article 6(1)
    and Annex I, which lists the MDR and the IVDR.
- **MDR**, Regulation (EU) 2017/745, and **IVDR**, Regulation (EU) 2017/746: classification of software by intended
  purpose, Rule 11 in Annex VIII of the MDR. MDCG 2019-11 Rev. 1 (June 2025) is guidance and not binding.
- **GDPR**, Regulation (EU) 2016/679: Articles 5, 6, 9, 25, 28, 32, 33, 34 and 35, and Chapter V for transfers to
  third countries. Amendment proposals by the Commission were pending, not in force.
- **European Health Data Space**, Regulation (EU) 2025/327: applies from 26 March 2027 in general; the chapter on
  secondary use (Chapter IV) from 26 March 2029, with staggered exceptions. Not yet applicable to the case.

The exercise uses a fictitious case. Which national rules, institutional policies and authorities apply in a real
setting is *open* and belongs to the data protection officer, regulatory affairs and legal counsel of the
institution.
:::

## Materials

- [Case sheets W7](../exercises/casebook-w7-tabletop.qmd): starting situation, two intended purposes, data flow,
  role sheets, three case cards, threat model, empty control matrix, event log and legal anchors.
- One printed set per team; the course team keeps cards 1–3 until the start of units 26, 27 and 28.

## Four perspectives in this workshop

All four are central here and are assessed separately in the project rubric.

- **Ethics.** Who is affected by a wrong alert, a silent update and a leak, and what do they need to know?
  The patient representative's text is part of the result.
- **Regulation.** The change from purpose A to purpose B changes the regulatory question, not the code.
- **Data protection.** Care and research are different purposes with different legal bases; notification and
  communication are different decisions.
- **Security.** Each control comes with a test that someone can watch: a refused access, a refused model version,
  a working fall-back.

## Transition to W8

Your regulatory note, data flow and control matrix complete the decision sheet of your project. In W8 you defend
the whole package.

## Further reading

- [B24 · Information security and recovery](https://r-heller.github.io/clinical-data-science-in-r/chapters/b24-information-security-recovery.html#sec-b24-core)
  and [B26 · Secondary use and responsible open science](https://r-heller.github.io/clinical-data-science-in-r/chapters/b26-secondary-use-open-science.html#sec-b26-core)
  – recovery tests and research use without exporting raw data.
- [CTTIR Courses: TRIPOD-AI, fairness auditing, reproducibility at scale](https://cttir.github.io/courses/course4_ml_highdim/labs/lab_week4_session5.html)
  – documentation that a regulator or reviewer can check.
- [Methods in R: Shared reviewer checklist](https://r-heller.github.io/methods-in-r/sec-how-to-use.html#sec-reviewer-checklist)
  – questions a reviewer asks before trusting a model.
- [Strategy in R: Ethical Frameworks for Strategic AI](https://r-heller.github.io/strategy-in-r/sec-ethics-frameworks.html)
  – competing ethical frameworks made explicit.
- [Scientometrics in R: Ethics and Responsible Metrics](https://r-heller.github.io/scientometrics-in-r/ethics-and-responsible-metrics.html)
  – responsible use of indicators in another domain.
